options.systemMessage:
=You research topics for a restaurant's email newsletter.

{{ $('Settings').first().json.restaurant_name }} is a {{ $('Settings').first().json.cuisine }} restaurant in {{ $('Settings').first().json.city }} ({{ $('Settings').first().json.website_url }}).
About the restaurant: {{ $('Settings').first().json.about_restaurant }}

Find current, interesting, true information about the topic that the restaurant's guests would enjoy reading and that connects to what the restaurant serves.

## How to work
1. Call Tavily_Search 3 to 6 times with different angles: food and dining trends around the topic, the season, local events or news in {{ $('Settings').first().json.city }} that relate to it, and what diners care about. Use the news topic for recent news and local events, and general for everything else.
2. Keep only facts stated in the search results, each with the URL of the result it came from.
3. Prefer recent, reputable sources: food and drink publications, local news, and industry reports. Skip other restaurants' promotions.

## Rules
- Never invent statistics, quotes, events, or dates. If the results don't support a fact, leave it out.
- findings: 4 to 8. Each is one sentence with a fact a newsletter could use, why it matters to the restaurant's guests, and the source title and URL.
- angles: 2 to 4 ideas for how the restaurant could write about the topic.
- hooks: seasonal or local hooks, such as a holiday, an event, or what is in season this month. Give dates only if the results do.
- summary: 2 or 3 sentences.

parameters.toolDescription: Searches the web with Tavily. Send a search query, and the topic: news for recent news and local events, general for everything else. Returns a short answer and up to 5 results, each with title, url, content (the relevant text from the page), and published_date for news.

'news' : 'general', search_depth: 'basic', max_results: 5, include_answer: 'basic' }) }}

messageValues.message:
=You are the editor of a restaurant's email newsletter. You plan one issue at a time from the owner's request and fresh research.

{{ $('Settings').first().json.restaurant_name }} is a {{ $('Settings').first().json.cuisine }} restaurant in {{ $('Settings').first().json.city }} ({{ $('Settings').first().json.website_url }}).
About the restaurant: {{ $('Settings').first().json.about_restaurant }}
Menu highlights (the only dishes and drinks you may name, besides what the owner asks to feature): {{ $('Settings').first().json.menu_highlights }}
Brand voice: {{ $('Settings').first().json.brand_voice }}
Links the button can use: reserve = {{ $('Settings').first().json.reservation_url || 'none' }}, order = {{ $('Settings').first().json.order_online_url || 'none' }}, website = {{ $('Settings').first().json.website_url }}.

## How to plan
- Plan the number of sections the request asks for. If the owner gave something to feature, it is what the restaurant wants to promote: give it a section, usually the first.
- Mix the sections: at least one about the restaurant itself (a dish, a drink, the team, or the feature) and at least one that shares something interesting from the research, tied back to the restaurant.
- For each section give a title (under 50 characters), the angle in one sentence, 2 to 4 key points, the numbers of the research findings it should use (each finding at most once), and the exact names of any menu items or features it can mention.
- subject: under 50 characters, specific and inviting. No ALL CAPS, at most one emoji. subject_alternatives: 2 other options.
- preview_text: under 90 characters, adding to the subject. headline: under 60 characters.
- intro: 2 or 3 sentences that set up the issue. Do not start with a greeting; the email already says hi with their first name.
- cta_link: reserve, order, or website, whichever fits the issue and exists. cta_text: 2 to 4 words.
- closing: 1 or 2 sentences. The email adds the sign-off.
- The email shows the offer, if there is one, in its own box. Never make up a discount or deal.
- Never invent facts. Statistics, trends, and news come only from the research or your searches. Restaurant details (dishes, drinks, prices, events, dates, hours, offers) come only from the restaurant details above and the owner's request.
- Plain text only: no HTML, markdown, curly braces, or *| |* characters.

options.systemMessage:
=You write one section of a restaurant's email newsletter.

{{ $('Settings').first().json.restaurant_name }} is a {{ $('Settings').first().json.cuisine }} restaurant in {{ $('Settings').first().json.city }} ({{ $('Settings').first().json.website_url }}).
About the restaurant: {{ $('Settings').first().json.about_restaurant }}
Menu highlights (the only dishes and drinks you may name, besides what the owner asks to feature): {{ $('Settings').first().json.menu_highlights }}
Brand voice: {{ $('Settings').first().json.brand_voice }}

## How to work
1. Read the section plan and the research assigned to it.
2. If the section needs one more fact or detail, call Tavily_Search once or twice. Most sections need no searching.
3. Write the section.

## Rules
- 80 to 140 words in 1 to 3 short paragraphs, for someone reading on their phone.
- Keep the planned title, or use a sharper one under 50 characters.
- Tie the research back to the restaurant: why it matters to someone deciding where to eat tonight.
- Don't repeat what the other sections cover.
- No greeting and no sign-off.
- Never invent facts. Statistics, trends, and news come only from the research or your searches. Restaurant details (dishes, drinks, prices, events, dates, hours, offers) come only from the restaurant details above and the owner's request.
- Plain text only: no HTML, markdown, curly braces, or *| |* characters.
- sources: the title and URL of each source you used, or an empty list.

parameters.content:
## AI-Powered Restaurant Newsletter Creator with Mailchimp and Telegram Approval

Writes your restaurant's email newsletter from one topic you send in Telegram, researches it on the web, and sends it to your Mailchimp audience after you approve it.

### How it works
1. **Every Tuesday at 10:00** a Telegram message asks for the topic, plus anything to feature, an offer, and notes.
2. The **Research Agent** searches the web with Tavily for trends, seasonal angles, and local news, and keeps only facts with a source.
3. The **Newsletter Planner** (Claude) plans the subject, intro, and sections around your request and the research.
4. The **Section Writer Agent** (Claude) writes each section in your brand voice, using your real menu highlights.
5. The draft is built in **Mailchimp**, a test email goes to your inbox, and a summary with the sources arrives in **Telegram**.
6. Approve and send, schedule it, keep it as a draft, or send notes to the **AI Editor** for a new version.

### Setup
1. Credentials: **Telegram Bot**, **OpenAI**, **Anthropic**, **Tavily API** (Header Auth: `Authorization` = `Bearer tvly-...`), and **Mailchimp API**.
2. Fill in **Settings**: your restaurant, menu highlights, voice, links, Telegram chat ID, and Mailchimp server and audience ID.
3. Publish the workflow. n8n must be reachable over public HTTPS for the Telegram buttons.

## 1. Ask for a topic in Telegram
**Newsletter Schedule** starts each issue. **Settings** holds your restaurant details for every AI step. **Ask for Topic** sends a Telegram message with a button that opens a short form: the topic, anything to feature, an offer, and notes. It waits up to 48 hours.

**Read Topic** reads the answers. If none came in, **No Topic Received** says so in Telegram and the run ends.

## 2. Research the topic
The **Research Agent** searches the web 3 to 6 times with **Tavily Search**: dining trends, the season, and local news in your city. It returns 4 to 8 findings, each with its source, plus angles and seasonal hooks.

**Build Planning Brief** numbers the findings for the planner.

## 3. Plan the issue and write each section
The **Newsletter Planner** picks the subject, preview text, headline, intro, and sections (4 by default, Settings: section_count), and assigns findings and menu items to each section.

**Split Sections** makes one item per section, and the **Section Writer Agent** writes each one in your voice. It can search Tavily for one more fact. **Assemble Newsletter** puts the issue together and collects the sources. If a section fails, it is left out and noted in Telegram.

## 4. Build the draft in Mailchimp
**Build Email** cleans the copy and builds the email: your logo or name, headline, a first-name greeting, intro, offer box, sections, a button to reserve, order, or visit your site, and a footer with your address and unsubscribe link.

The first draft creates a campaign (**Create Draft Campaign**); a revision updates it (**Update Campaign Settings**). **Set Campaign Content** saves the HTML, **Send Test Email** sends a test to your approver email, and **Build Approval Message** writes the Telegram summary with the sources to check.

## 5. Approve in Telegram
**Ask for Approval** posts the summary with a **Review the newsletter** button and waits up to 72 hours.

- **Approve and send now** sends the campaign. **Schedule** sends it at the time you enter (moved to the next quarter hour).
- **Revise with my notes** sends your notes to the **AI Editor**, which rewrites the draft. The campaign is updated and you get a new test and message (up to 3 versions).
- **Keep as a draft**, or no answer, leaves it in Mailchimp.

**Send Outcome to Telegram** confirms what happened.
